comments.text:
Gratitude for the virginians who are keeping good clean energy practices, gratitude for the government of virginia, gratitude for an increased visibility of respect for environmentalism in virginia's culture.

part of that respect for environmentalism comes down to listening to native tribes and respecting their guidance and boundaries in acts to visibly make up for and erase some of the mistreatment and pain in the past within native/pilgrim relations. 

I am encouraging virginians to give native americans a greater respect and to empower their influence more to see the greater success, I am making virginians mindful that the 'ghost' of native american hardship and landswiping hangs over virginia, it will cause trouble and mischief in the land for non natives who have treated the land with less gratitude and less respect until there is a stronger movement to restore the power of the tribes and to give them what the treaties promise and more.

One example of this is the Chesapeake Bay Program in Virginia operating outside of its own parameters by reportedly largely ignoring the voices of the seven tribes that it was working with and who were marked by it's mission statement as a key part of what the CBP was created to make manifest. 

I am asking for the CBP and for virginians in general to try to bow deeper to the native tribes and to keep visible and in practice respect for them in the coming years, and I am very grateful they comply. SINCERITY IS WHAT MATTERS
